title: VERIFICATION OF SMALL SATELLITE FITNESS FOR PURPOSE IN NEW APPLICATION DOMAINS - EXPRO+
description: Private investment has stimulated the development of several new small satellite systems within Europe over the last five years. These exploit the reduced technical risk associated with technologies coming from previous ESA and Member State funded developments and benefiting from parallel technology improvements (eg miniaturization, materials etc) so that standard commercial practices can be followed.However, in many cases the privately financed and operated satellites include technical characteristics that create the potential for exploitation in other user domains where there is less acceptance of EO or where technical effort would be required to develop and verify the required information products and services. This may be due to the fact that the sensors are in some way unique or that the the overall system offers unique performance capabilities. Addressing this asymmetric risk structure is routinely practiced within ESA programmes however and given the connections ESA has with a wide range of stakeholders and the experience in supporting diverse EO applications development, ESA is well placed to fund the required developments up to the point where fitness for purpose is demonstrated for a well defined and clearly engaged stakeholder community which can then be the basis for private sector funded follow-on developments and customer engagement. This Invitation to Tender addresses this gap in order to generate an acceptable risk pattern for private sector investors (and the satellite operators) to support the necessary operationalization and commercialization activities. The overall objectives to be achieved are:(i) Accelerate the update of data, information and services from European small satellite operators among customer segments that cannot be effectively addressed by such private sector entities alone(ii) Verify, together with key organizations within the target customer segments, that data, information and services from the small satellite operators address an agreed set of priority issues/gaps and the demonstrated operational performance and processes are consistent with customer segment working practices and are therefore considered to be fit for purposeThis will require the contractor to engage a clear set of customers with requirements that cannot be presently addressed but which could be addressed by modifications to or with a small satellite system currently in operationIdentify a clear set of developments associated with the small satellite system in order to address the requirements of the stakeholders being targeted on a timeframe that is of immediate interest to the target stakeholdersElaborate verification exercises that enable a sufficiently convincing demonstration and verificationthat the developments executed have resulted in the enhanced small satellite system being capable to provide the required information under actual operational conditions to a performance level that is considered acceptable and within working practices that are compliant with the stakeholders operational environment. This should include a clear definition as to what are these threshold performance levels as well as a credible prospect of follow-on commercial uptake if these agreed performance levels are sufficiently well achievedIdentify follow-on mechanisms that can credibly support a transition to full commercial uptake

description: The objective of the activity is to develop a highly integrated, scalable Ku or Ka-band TX/RX direct radiating array, for versatileconnectivity missions in low earth orbit. Critical breadboarding will be carried out, levering the advances in Mm-wave silicon technologies and advanced packaging techniques to achieve a high degree of integration. Targeted Improvements: Enabling highly integrated combined transmit and receive active antenna with a large number of elements, for low earth orbit applications, not existing today. Description: Mm-wave silicon technologies together with advanced packaging and printed circuit board technologies are the key enablers of high-volume active antennas today. To achieve the equivalent isotropic radiated power (EIRP) required by LEO constellationsatellites, power levels of up to 20dBm are needed in 2000+ element class arrays. At the same time, noise figure levels approaching1dB at Ka band can significantly improve the performance of next generation arrays. Multibeam beamforming operation can be obtainedby several beamforming strategies that have only been possible thanks to the recent advancements in silicon technologies. To allow affordable high-volume manufacturing of reliable arrays, packaging and PCB integration are of equal importance as the semiconductor technology itself and they all need to be considered in co-design. This activity will develop in a first step a scalable Ku- or Ka-band direct array transmit and receive architecture taking into account aspects including beamforming, low noise and high-efficiency power amplification, filtering, control, switching, interconnections, PCB routing and thermal control. Mm-wave silicon technologies and packaging techniques will be reviewed, and a technology baseline will be selected for all critical antenna elements. Thermal management and spacecraft accommodation will be taken into account to maximise integration. In a second step a sub-array breadboard with radiating elements will be designed manufactured and tested. The breadboard shall be sufficient to evaluate the functionality of the direct radiating architecture and to test the RF and thermal management concept.

Työkalun tulee pystyä tarjoamaan arvio kartalle tuodun tai piirretyn linjaston kalustomäärästä, ajokilometreistä ja -tunneista, lähtömääristä, matkustajapotentiaalista ja saavutettavuudesta erilaiseen dataan peilaten (esimerkiksi väestötiedot ja -ennusteet sekä kävelyetäisyydet pysäkeille). Työkalulla tulee olemaan HSL:ssä arviolta noin 60 käyttäjää (tarjoajan täytyy kuitenkin tarjota rajaton määrä käyttöoikeuksia HSL:n työntekijöille (ml. henkilökohtaiset ja -yhteiskäyttäjätilit) ja tarvittaessa kuntayhteistyössä myös kuntien työntekijöille ja sidosryhmille ilman lisämaksua sopimuskauden ajan).
